title: AI-Based Spark Job Performance Optimization System
tagline: Teaching Spark to configure itself — 72% faster, 0.976 R².
description: An XGBoost-driven recommendation engine that learns from historical PySpark execution parameters and outputs optimized job configurations, reducing runtime and infrastructure cost for data engineering teams.
problem: Data engineering teams tune Spark job configurations largely by hand, spending manual effort per job run while still leaving execution time and infrastructure spend on the table across enterprise-scale workloads.
solution: I built an ML pipeline that learns from PySpark execution parameters and outputs optimized job configurations automatically, packaged as a configurable module callable from existing pipeline orchestration tools.
contribution: Designed and built the full pipeline end to end: feature engineering from Spark execution logs, model training and hyperparameter tuning, validation methodology, and integration as a callable module.
results: Cut Spark job execution time by 64–72%, measured across three enterprise-scale workload profiles
Achieved R² = 0.976 on job runtime forecasting, validated on a held-out production-mirroring test set
Reduced infrastructure cost exposure by cutting manual configuration effort per job run

title: Document Intelligence System
tagline: Question-answering over 400+ pages of unstructured documents.
description: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline enabling question answering over large, unstructured document corpora, built with multi-stage chunking, embedding generation, and semantic retrieval.
problem: Real regulatory and technical documents run hundreds of pages, making it slow and error-prone to find answers manually across structured and unstructured sources.
solution: I designed an ingestion, preprocessing, and retrieval pipeline with multi-stage chunking and semantic retrieval using LangChain and the Groq API, plus a reranking step to sharpen retrieval precision.
contribution: Built the RAG pipeline end to end — chunking strategy, embedding generation, semantic retrieval, and the reranking optimization loop — and evaluated it with RAGAS metrics.
results: Increased document QA response relevance by 18%, measured via RAGAS evaluation metrics
Enabled question answering over 400+ page unstructured document corpora, tested on real regulatory and technical documents
Improved retrieval precision through reranking, validated with automated scoring

title: Cardiovascular Disease Prediction
tagline: 68,000 patient records, one interpretable risk score.
description: An end-to-end predictive analytics system for cardiovascular disease detection, built on supervised machine learning with clinically relevant feature engineering and SHAP-based interpretability.
problem: Cardiovascular disease risk needs to be predicted reliably from patient records, but clinical adoption also requires model decisions to be interpretable rather than a black box.
solution: I built a supervised ML system trained on 68,000 cleaned patient records, with clinically relevant feature engineering, rigorous cross-validation, and SHAP explanations layered on top of the final classifiers.
contribution: Owned the full pipeline: data preprocessing, feature engineering, feature selection, model evaluation, 10-fold cross-validation, and threshold tuning for the XGBoost and CatBoost classifiers.
results: Trained and validated on 68,000 cleaned patient records with 10-fold cross-validation
Achieved 0.803 ROC-AUC, 83.0% Recall, and 74.2% F1-score after threshold tuning
Delivered interpretable, AI-driven predictions using SHAP

title: Password Strength Analyzer
tagline: Hybrid machine learning system for intelligent password security assessment.
description: A password security analyzer that combines a hybrid LSTM model, rule-based heuristics, breach detection, entropy-based crack-time estimation, and secure password generation to evaluate password strength.
problem: Traditional password strength checks rely mainly on fixed rules such as length and character diversity, which can miss common patterns, leaked credentials, and predictable password structures.
solution: I built a hybrid password security system that combines character-level LSTM modeling with numerical password features, rule-based analysis, Have I Been Pwned breach detection using k-anonymity, and entropy-based crack-time estimation. The system fuses these signals into a single strength score with actionable feedback.
contribution: Built the end-to-end password analysis pipeline, including feature engineering, sequential password encoding, hybrid LSTM architecture, rule-based scoring, HIBP k-anonymity integration, score fusion, crack-time estimation, and secure password generation.
results: Combined ML-based pattern analysis with deterministic security rules and breach intelligence into a unified 0–100 password strength score
Evaluated passwords using character-level patterns and six numerical features including length, digits, uppercase, lowercase, and special-character counts
Implemented privacy-preserving HIBP breach checks using SHA-1 hash prefixes rather than transmitting the full password or hash
Added entropy-based brute-force crack-time estimation and actionable recommendations for improving weak passwords
